decisions.claim: Off Linux, profilesPath() and legacy.profiles() are the same file, so --migrate --finish deletes the ACTIVE store
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED and the most serious finding of the round - a data-loss bug created by MY OWN platform fix two commits earlier. Off Linux systemRoot() returns userRoot(), so source and destination collapse to one path; every agent then reads as 'already across', nothing is pending, and cleanup shreds the store the running daemon is using, reporting a successful migration. Both status() and cleanup() now refuse off Linux with an explanation, since there is genuinely nothing to migrate there.

decisions.claim: shredViewer skips the unlink when the random overwrite throws, and reports success
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED. The overwrite and the unlink shared one try block, so an allocation failure on randomBytes(size) - plausible for a large log on a small machine - swallowed the error and left the complete readable page behind. The unlink is the point and now happens regardless; the overwrite is best-effort in its own block.

decisions.claim: execFileSync for the browser blocks the loop that runs the cleanup timer and signal handlers
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED by inspection. xdg-open can wait on a browser helper; if that helper ignores the timeout signal the call never returns, ctrl-C cannot run the JS handler, and the plaintext page stays on disk - the exact outcome the ephemeral design exists to prevent. Now a detached, unref'd spawn. Re-verified that the page is still shredded.

decisions.claim: Cleanup identifies the viewer only by pathname, so one invocation can shred another's kept page
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED. Fixed with an identity stamp taken at write time - and the first attempt using the inode ALONE was caught by its own test: unlinking a file frees its inode and the next create is routinely handed the same number back, so a genuinely different file matched. The stamp pairs inode with mtime.
